title: Business succession or sale planning
summary: The largest financial event of most business owners' lives. Plan 5–10 years out.
detailsHtml:
The four primary exit paths

Family transition: Pass to children or family members. Tax-advantaged through gifting, GRATs, sales to intentionally defective grantor trusts, etc. Often emotional and operationally complex; many family transitions fail because the next generation doesn't share the founder's commitment.

Sale to employees (ESOP or management buyout): Employee Stock Ownership Plans offer significant tax advantages. Under §1042, a C-corp owner can defer gain on the sale by reinvesting in qualified replacement property — but four conditions apply: (1) the corporation must be a C-corp at the time of sale (not S-corp); (2) the owner must have held the shares for at least 3 years; (3) the ESOP must own at least 30% of the company immediately after the sale; (4) qualified replacement property (QRP — securities of domestic operating corporations, NOT mutual funds or bonds) must be purchased within a 15-month window (3 months before to 12 months after the sale). The deferral becomes permanent only if the QRP is held until death, at which point step-up in basis eliminates the deferred gain. Selling QRP during life triggers recognition. Separately, S-corp ESOPs can be tax-exempt at the corporate level on ESOP-owned portions under §512(e), a different regime. Both structures are complex and expensive to set up (~$200K+) but compelling for the right business.

Sale to strategic or financial buyer: Highest typical valuation, but requires the business to be in saleable condition (clean financials, systematized operations, reduced owner dependence). 12–24 month process. Net proceeds after taxes and fees typically 60–75% of headline sale price.

Wind-down: If the business has no transferable value, gradual reduction in operations. Often the only realistic option for highly owner-dependent service businesses.

The 5-year preparation timeline

Year -5 to -3: Build the management layer. Document systems. Diversify customer base. Reduce owner dependency.

Year -3 to -2: Audited or reviewed financials. Sell-side QofE (quality of earnings) preparation. Tax planning for sale (entity structure, salary normalization, working capital optimization).

Year -1 to 0: Engage M&A advisor or broker. Manage the process. Negotiate working capital adjustments, escrow, indemnifications, non-competes.
